items.title: Building with Nature in Mind: A Practical Technology Checklist
items.excerpt: I’m trying to judge technology by the job it does, not by how new it is. This is the checklist I use to think through local needs, maintenance, data, energy use and side effects before choosing a tool.

items.title: How to Choose a Laptop for Real Work in 2026
items.excerpt: My work calls for coding, Linux, networking tools and virtual machines. This guide covers the specifications I would prioritize and what to verify before buying in India.

items.title: The Greenest Upgrade May Be the One You Do Not Buy
items.excerpt: Before replacing a slow laptop or phone, I would check the actual symptom, back up important data, and look at repair options. A new device may be the right answer, but it shouldn’t be the first assumption.

items.title: Passkeys, Recovery, and the Human Side of Security
items.excerpt: Passkeys improve the sign-in step, but they don’t remove the need to protect recovery paths. This guide looks at what to prepare before a phone, device or credential manager becomes unavailable.

items.title: How I Decide Whether a Task Needs AI
items.excerpt: I don’t start by asking which AI model to use. I start with the result I need, the cost of a mistake, and whether a simpler tool or a person would do the job better.

items.title: Better Light Begins by Protecting the Dark
items.excerpt: When I think about outdoor lighting, I start with the job: what needs to be visible, for whom, and at what time? These notes cover aiming, brightness, controls and spill, without assuming that more light is always better.

items.title: A Soil Sensor Is a Question, Not an Answer
items.excerpt: A soil-moisture sensor describes conditions near its probe, not an entire field. I’d treat a reading as one input and check it against placement, soil, crop conditions and an irrigation log before setting thresholds.

items.title: What Soil Can Teach Us About Measurement
items.excerpt: A sensor gives me a reading, not the full story. These notes are about context, uncertainty and why numbers need to be checked against the place and the decision they’re meant to support.

items.title: Before I Build With AI, I Ask Who Carries the Risk
items.excerpt: Before I add AI to a feature, I ask who it helps, what data it needs, what happens if it is wrong, and how a person can challenge the result.

items.title: Security Is a Form of Care
items.excerpt: I approach security as a way to reduce avoidable harm, not a contest in technical capability. These notes focus on permissions, recovery, privacy and the everyday choices that make systems safer to use.
